name: Hippo

app.note: The head height of the red fox, the size that the user chose for the cat, the dog, and the panda: the scale puts the standing skull top (the highest vertex within 0.03 u of the middle plane, 0.9807 u) at 1.570 m, 1.600907 m for each unit, with the standing shoulder joints at 0.888504 m (the entry of the hippo in ANIMALS). The parametric hippo of main stood 1.462 m high to the head top. The reach is the reach of the arm factor below, from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm. With no --check, pnpm rig-mesh stops until the arm factor gives this reach.

armFactorNote: The factor of the upper arm and the forearm. The arms of the mesh are short: 0.369 m from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm with no factor, 0.62 of the trunk from the hips joint to the shoulder joints. With 1.5, the reach is 0.539 m, and the arm is 0.94 of the trunk, as the red fox (0.91) and the dog (0.92); the panda has 1.497. The parametric hippo of main had arms of 0.734 m. The user called the arms of the dog with the factor 1.75 much too long, so the contrabass of the hippo is smaller (bassScale 0.8 of src/models/species.ts), and the hold brings it to the arms (docs/decisions/2026-10-18-mesh-hippo.md).
legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh. The hippo stands at its contrabass in the app, as the hippos of the reference images, so no seat asks for longer legs. The seat of the legs of the seated bind is 0.139 m.
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the top of the ears, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-18-hippo-mesh/: sections.py gives the cuts at each height (sections-y.txt, sections-x.txt, sections-z.txt), and measures.py the parts (measures.txt). The legs are short stumps apart below the crotch at y 0.122, with the middle of each leg at x 0.123 and z -0.05. The thigh joint lies a little below the crotch, the knee and the ankle divide the stump, and the toes lie at the ball of the foot (toe tip at z 0.075). The round belly reaches z 0.216 at y 0.35. The trunk joints lie 0.01 to 0.02 behind the middle of the body cut. The hippo has no neck: the head starts at the chin at y 0.70, and the neck joint lies below it. The cuts across the free arm (arm-axis.txt) give its middle line: the arm is apart from the body from x 0.207 out. The shoulder joint lies on that line where it meets x 0.19, inside the root, the elbow halfway to the wrist on the middle line, the wrist at the narrowest cut before the paw, and the finger joint 0.03 before the tip of the paw. The ear joint lies at the root of the small ear on the top of the head, and its tail at the ear tip. The small tail hangs down under the buttock from its root at y 0.215 to its tip at y 0.157. The palm takes the smallest principal direction of the vertices of the left paw beyond the wrist, inward, down, and back (paw.py). The paw is round, so the two smaller spreads are close (0.152 and 0.144).

studio.note: The studio has no hippo. legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it. The posture is the seated posture of design 5.2: the thigh slopes 25 degrees down from the hip to the knee, the thighs turn 15 degrees out, and the shin is vertical (docs/research/2026-10-16-hip-open/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0). The source shin slants 8.5 degrees forward. The foot and the toes keep the turn of the source, so that the soles stay flat on the foot ring. The trunk shares and the bind arms are the values of the cat, the dog, and the panda.

sliver.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, and the panda. The rule takes 23 faces in 13 groups.

line.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, and the panda. The rule takes 100 corners.

weights.clavicleMiddleNote: The share of the clavicle weight that a vertex below headFrom keeps grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to 1 at the larger distance (units), and the chest takes the rest. Bone heat gave the chest under the chin weights of both clavicles (0.12 to 0.21). The bow arm turns the right clavicle far, so faces 617 and 618 on the middle plane folded in each play sample. A narrow fade (0.02 to 0.06, 0.04 to 0.10, 0.08 to 0.18) moved the fold to the faces of the fade, and a higher clavicleFrom to the front of the shoulder (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-chest/).
weights.armTopNote: The share of the clavicle and upper arm weights that a vertex gives to the neck grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units). With the narrow fade 0.64 to 0.68, face 116 at the back of the right shoulder joined a corner of the clavicle and the upper arm to two corners of the neck, and it folded in 13.7% of the play samples. With 0.625 to 0.7, the fade spans more rings of faces, and face 116 folds in no sample. The fade is sensitive: with 0.61, 0.615, 0.6, or 0.62 to 0.69, the relax of a shape of raise fails, and 44% to 99.8% of the play samples fold (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-arms.md).
weights.rigidNote: The face nearest to each point (source units) takes the mean of the weights of its corners, and the faces of a list of points take one mean. Face 323 joins the head, the neck, and a corner with a clavicle weight of 0.51 at the back of the right side of the neck, and it folded in each play sample when the bow arm turned the clavicle forward. The point is its source middle (pnpm fold-probe bassist --faces). Face 1498 of the left wrist, a thin face across the joint, stayed turned after the relax of the shape of the bent wrist and folded in nearly each sample of the play, the lift, and the rest. Face 51 of the right paw, a thin face across the joint of the fingers, folded in each rest sample, and with the level elbow of the play in 41% of the play samples. Face 463 at the front of the right shoulder folded in 22% of the play samples. With the mean weights, none of the three folds. The same rule on face 116 at the back of the right shoulder folded faces 125 and 241 of the neck in nearly each sample, and on face 52 of the right paw it moved the fold back to face 51, because face 52 shares two corners with face 51. The third item is a group: faces 51 and 52 take one mean of their four corners, and face 52, which folded in 11.6% of the play samples, folds in none (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-arms.md).

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the round haunch stays on the hips. It starts at the knee and ends at the crotch.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones: the cuts show the arm apart from the body from x 0.207 out (161 vertices of the free left arm). The belly is wider than that plane below the arm, so the free arm is the part beyond the plane that holds the finger tip. Above headFrom, each vertex follows the head only: the chin starts at y 0.70. earBase lies above the head, so the small ears follow the head. The small tail is a ball on one bone (tailBall): the vertices within radius of the center and behind the plane z = behind follow the tail. clavicleFrom, armTop, and shoulderHead are the rules of the panda, moved with the shoulder joint (y 0.555) and the wide neck of the hippo.

raise.note: The shape of the bow arm in the play of the bassist, with the mean turns of the samples in which face 323 folds (pnpm raise-fit bassist --faces 323 --side R): the clavicle turns 45 degrees forward, as the reach of the hold, and the upper arm 104.7 degrees from the bind. The fade covers 98% of the play samples. With the rule, faces 240, 286, and 480 of the front of the shoulder fold in 1% to 5% of the play samples (89%, 95%, and 37% before), and faces 477 and 461 of the upper arm, which turn over in the pose of the rule, in 93% and 34% (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-chest/fold-probe-base.txt).

The shape of the bent right elbow in the play of the bassist, with the mean turn of the forearm on the upper arm in the samples in which faces 232 and 233 of the inner elbow fold (pnpm raise-fit bassist --faces 232,233 --side R --bone forearm): the elbow bends 68.2 degrees, and the faces folded in 4.9% and 4.1% of the play samples. The rule turns only the forearm: with the turns of the clavicle and the upper arm of the fit, faces 463, 336, and 337 of the chest folded in up to 10% of the play samples. It takes the place of the shape of the left arm for face 1356, which changed no fold since the left elbow points down (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-arms.md).

The shape of the bow arm with the level elbow of the play (pnpm raise-fit bassist --faces 517,244,116 --side R with the elbow poles of HIPPO_HOLD): the clavicle turns 50 degrees forward, as the reach of the hold, and the upper arm 91.6 degrees from the bind. With the level elbow, face 517 at the back of the right shoulder folded in each play sample, and the first rule of the right arm, fit for the raised elbow, did not relax it. In the pose of the rule, face 517 turns over and relaxes in 1 round (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-arms.md).

The shape of the bent left wrist on the neck (pnpm raise-fit bassist --faces 2201,1495 --side L --bone hand): the paw turns 163.1 degrees on the forearm in the mean of the samples, nearly a twist around the forearm, and faces 2201 and 1495 of the wrist folded in each sample of the play, the lift, and the rest. The rule turns 10 degrees further on the same axis. In the pose of the rule, face 1498 stays turned after the relax, also with grow 1 or below 0.5 (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-arms.md).

cut.note: The thin faces under each armpit join the upper arm to the chest. On the right, faces 462, 248, 249, 477, and 461 folded in 74% to 100% of the play samples, and weight rules and shapes only moved the folds (docs/decisions/2026-10-19-hippo-chest.md). Below the height top (source units), the faces with a corner in the free arm and a corner in the body go: 16 on the left, 14 on the right. The same number of new faces close the arm and the trunk, and no vertex moves. The arm and the trunk stay joined above the top, 0.015 u below the shoulder joint, as for the beaver. At top 0.50 and 0.52, face 462 folded in each play sample, and at 0.55 and 0.56, the neck and the chest folded more (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-arms.md).

flip.note: The values of the fox, the rabbit, the cat, the dog, and the panda. The rule flips 13 edges.

refine.ringsNote: The rig has no rings. A ring at each elbow puts the rig at 3,211 triangles, above the budget of 3,200 of a studio body (the mesh has 3,141 triangles), so the long thin faces 753 of the left upper arm and 30 of the right upper arm stay (rig-rings.log). A ring at the left wrist cuts 32 edges and puts the rig at 3,205 triangles (docs/research/2026-10-19-hippo-arms.md).

check.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, and the panda.

tone.note: The mesh has warmer colors than the hippo of the reference images and of SPECIES_COLORS.hippo (#8f7d83, Oklab hue 356 degrees): the plain fur faces have the hue 12 degrees and the chroma 0.031, and the pale belly and muzzle the hue 50 degrees and the chroma 0.047 (fur-colors.txt). The skin of the reference hippos of orchestra-latest.png has the hue 356 to 7 degrees and the chroma 0.027 to 0.040 (render-colors.txt). As the user chose for the panda, each plain face takes the hue and the chroma of the species color of its band and keeps its lightness: a row is [L, dL, da, db] in Oklab, the fur (L 0.58) moves to the fur color, and the belly (L 0.87) to the belly color #b8a3a6. The claws keep their colors. In the front view of the gallery, the fur then has the hue 32 degrees and the chroma 0.045, and the belly the hue 38 degrees and the chroma 0.044, against 31 and 0.044, and 35 and 0.043, of the parametric hippo of main (render-colors.txt).

colors.note: The values of samples, palette, dark, and eyeShare are the values of the other meshes. A dark face in the eye box is a face of an eye: 3 faces on the left and 4 on the right, at x 0.062 to 0.076, y 0.908 to 0.917, and z 0.092 to 0.096, far back on the head (head-colors.txt). The config has no nose box: the export takes each gloss shell out of the middle plane as an eye, and the hippo has two nostrils, no nose pad, so the nostrils keep the fur, and the export takes the front of the muzzle as the tip of the nose.

eyeShell.note: The values of the fox, the cat, and the dog. The old eye of each side is its dark faces and the faces around them: 10 faces on each side. They take the color of 49% (left) and 24% (right) of the area of the faces around them.

chair.note: The chair of the rig sets the seat top of the seated bind under the haunch. The short thighs lie under the belly, so the seat ends behind them (front edge at z -0.1 u, the shins from z -0.095 u). The hippo stands in the app (the standing pose of the rig, soloist of ANIMALS), so no player sits on this seat. The side view of the underside of the haunch is 15.1 cm above the seat top behind the hip joints, where the round haunch leaves the small seat.

crease.note: The values of the cat, the dog, and the panda. The seam has 35 vertices, and 185 vertices move.

sit.note: The values of the panda: 127 vertices of the haunch move down, at most 0.03 u.
